_comment: 3. The handoff, undone: ridgeback_1 loads the notebook onto jackal_1,
the jackal drives to the kitchen, and the ridgeback then tries to take
the cargo back -- TOO_FAR, because unload_from is gated on reach like
every other hand verb (_require_carrier -> _require_near, GATE_CARRY).
The two robots are team_1, and the sequencing is by tick count because
that is the only tool there is (open defect 5). Sized from the measured
costs -- grasp ~11 ticks, navigate ~100 + 10 per metre:
t=0     ridgeback_1 navigates to the notebook and grasps it (~145)
jackal_1 waits 300, so it does not arrive before there is
anything to load
t~300   jackal_1 navigates to ridgeback_1 (~130) and waits 300
t~545   ridgeback_1 loads the notebook onto jackal_1 -- in reach,
because the jackal came to it
t~730   jackal_1 drives to the kitchen refrigerator, cargo aboard
t~1145  ridgeback_1 asks for it back. The jackal is two rooms away.
The ridgeback cannot follow: its base locks the moment its arm is loaded
and it unloads to a full hand, so there is no version of this it can
recover from by driving -- which is what makes the handoff a commitment
rather than a loan.
Run with coop2/team_layouts/s1/sets_3.json (9 robots) on v4_s1_v4_lh.
Expect on ridgeback_1's last action:
PRE_CONDITION_ERROR: You are N.NN m from jackal_1, too far to unload
from it (you must be within N.NN m). Navigate to it first.

ridgeback_1.task: hand it over, then ask for it back

jackal_1.task: fetch the cargo and drive off with it
